clue.text: Cut short conversation, quietly leaving fellow dancing

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its final letter, here the chat's closing letter

parts.note: a chat is a conversation

indicators.note: the quiet letter is leaving the word for fellow, so it is taken out

parts.note: a chap is a fellow
P (piano) is the musical abbreviation for quietly

explanation.surface: A chat with a man is abruptly ended as he slips quietly away to dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut short' drops the last letter of CHAT; 'leaving' takes P out of CHAP. The two halves are identical, matching the dance's doubled name.
explanation.definitionFit: The cha-cha is a Latin ballroom dance, so the answer names a kind of dancing.

clue.text: One often dealt with dodgy veto in TUC procedure

parts.note: playing cards are dealt out to players

indicators.note: dodgy means unsound or suspect, so the letters of veto are rearranged

explanation.surface: A suspicious veto is handled in the course of a trade union meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: The TUC is the Trades Union Congress, the British federation of trade unions; at its conferences unions cast block votes by holding up cards.
explanation.definitionFit: In a card vote each union delegation's ballot carries its full membership, the standard voting method at the union congress.
